title: SMILE Pro: The Next Frontier (VisuMax 800)
summary: SMILE Pro represents the latest evolution in lenticule extraction, utilizing the 2 MHz VisuMax 800 femtosecond laser. This system enhances surgical precision through robotic assistance, ultra-fast laser frequency, and sophisticated cyclotorsion and centration compensation.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: SMILE (Small Incision Lenticule Extraction) Pro is the advanced iteration of the flapless refractive procedure. Using the VisuMax 800, a refractive lenticule is created within the intact corneal stroma and extracted through a microscopic 2-3mm incision. This preserves the biomechanical integrity of the anterior corneal lamellae and reduces post-operative dry eye.

branches: CentraLign: Assisted centration based on corneal vertex
OcuLign: Easy cyclotorsion compensation for astigmatism
Comfort: Faster cut reduces suction loss risk

sections.title: Clinical Indications
content: Myopia: -0.50 D to -10.00 D
Astigmatism: Up to -5.00 D (Cylinder)
Stable refraction for at least 12 months
Pachymetry: Sufficient residual stromal bed (>250μm)
Contact lens holiday: 1 week soft, 3 weeks hard lenses
Patients active in sports (no flap displacement risk)

sections.title: Contraindications & Warnings
content: Ectasia risk (Abnormal topography/Keratoconus)
Unstable refractive error
Severe Dry Eye Disease (DED) or OSD
History of Herpetic Keratitis
Pregnancy or Lactation
Autoimmune connective tissue diseases
Thin Cornea (Estimated RSB < 250 microns)

sections.title: Comprehensive Pre-Op Workup
content: Step 1: Manifest and Cycloplegic Refraction (Crucial for accuracy)
Step 2: Corneal Topography & Tomography (Pentacam/Galilei to rule out ectasia)
Step 3: Pachymetry (Confirm stromal thickness maps)
Step 4: Epithelial Thickness Mapping (Detect early keratoconus)
Step 5: Ocular Surface Assessment (TBUT, Schirmer test, MMP-9)
Step 6: Pupil Evaluation (Photopic vs. Scotopic sizes)
Step 7: Fundoscopy (Peripheral retinal exam to rule out breaks/lattice)

sections.title: The 10-Second Surgical Process
content: 1. Docking: Contact glass centration on the visual axis.
2. Suction: Activated at the touch of a button.
3. Posterior Surface: Laser creates the back of the lenticule.
4. Lenticule Side-cut: Defines the refractive edge.
5. Anterior Surface: Laser creates the front (cap) interface.
6. Entry Incision: 2mm tunnel created for extraction.
7. Extraction: Manual dissection and removal with forceps.

content.explanation: S: Suction stability (Don't rush). M: Menu check (Verify refraction). I: Identify planes (Posterior then Anterior). L: Lenticule integrity (Ensure no fragments). E: Ease of extraction (Gentle manipulation).

sections.title: Complications & Management
content: Opaque Bubble Layer (OBL): Minimize with energy settings
Black Spots: Ensure contact glass is clean
Difficult Extraction: Check for 'sticky' bridges
Cap Tear: Manage with 10-0 nylon if peripheral/large
Lenticule Fragment: High-mag slit lamp inspection
DLK (Sands of Sahara): Frequent topical steroids (q1h)
Transient Light Sensitivity (TLSS): Seen with high energy

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always dissect the POSTERIOR plane first to avoid losing the lenticule in the roof.
Use a 'Chansue' or 'Tan' dissector for smooth interface separation.
Ensure the 'White Ring Sign' is visible to confirm full lenticule separation.
Higher laser energy = Easier dissection but more OBL/DLK risk.
The VisuMax 800 robotic arm automatically swings away for easier extraction.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: Recent studies comparing SMILE Pro to standard SMILE show a significant reduction in suction loss (0.1% vs 0.8%) due to the decreased treatment time. The 'PRO' series also integrates with the ZEISS EQ Workplace, allowing for seamless digital planning. Landmark trials (e.g., Blum et al. 10-year data) show that lenticule extraction has long-term stability comparable to LASIK but with superior nerve regeneration and biomechanical endurance.
